newsitem.title: USA: CBOT raises soycomplex trading limits, margins.
newsitem.headline: CBOT raises soycomplex trading limits, margins.

text.p: The Chicago Board of Trade said it expanded trading limits for soybean, soyoil and soymeal futures to 150 percent of normal following limit gains in many contracts on Friday after the January USDA crop report.

From the start of trading in the day session on Monday, January 13, trading limits will be 45 cents per bushel for soybeans, $15 per ton for soymeal, and $.015 cent per lb for for soyoil futures. January 1997 contracts, now in delivery period, will continue to trade without daily limits.
The expanded limits will be in effect for a minimum two business days.
CBOT also raised margin requirements in line with the expanded limits. Initial margin to trade soybeans will become $2,025 per contract, soymeal $1,215, and soyoil $810.
